newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen futures touch new highs on JGB gains.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen futures touch new highs on JGB gains.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures edged towards new contract highs on Tuesday in line with Japanese government bond (JGB) futures amid continuing signs of weakness in Japan's economy.
Dealers said the interest rate futures were underpinned by losses in Nikkei markets, which ended weak despite Wall Street's recovery overnight.

Reports of another Japanese construction firm, Daito Kogyo Co Ltd, filing for court protection from creditors also lifted the market, as did growing confidence the U.S. Federal Reserve would leave rates steady at its policy meeting later in the day.
But dealers said the lead March Euroyen contract would have trouble extending its gains much further and attention was likely to shift to the June contract.
March Euroyen stood at its new contract high of 99.29 at 1110 GMT against its IMM close at 99.26.
September JGBs ended at 127.19 after hitting a high of 127.24 against a previous 126.97. Resistance is seen at 127.30.

Eurodollar futures ended easier but off their lows on declines in U.S. Treasuries after United Parcel Service (UPS) said it had reached a tentative pact with the Teamsters union to end a 15-day strike, which has hit the U.S. economy.
"Selling came in and volume picked up on the Eurodollars on reports UPS was reaching a settlement with the teamsters," a dealer at a U.S. futures house said.
December Eurodollars ended at 94.155 against their IMM close at 94.160. The more actively traded March contract ended at 94.110 against 94.120 after touching a low of 94.090.
"It seems like the Fed won't hike rates. U.S. economic indicators don't show any inflationary pressures," a trader at a Japanese institution said.

He said a rate hike would also damage the U.S. stock market, which was already suffering a bout of jitters after fears of lower corporate earnings triggered the Dow's second-biggest point drop in history last Friday.
